newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria denies renewed petrol shortage.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria denies renewed petrol shortage.

text.p: Nigeria's oil authorities criticised on Friday a new build up of queues for petrol in the commercial hub of Lagos, saying it had ample supplies of fuel.

"This is a rather disturbing development as the phenomena is baseless," the Pipelines and Products Marketing Company (PPMC), the arm of the state oil firm responsible for fuel supplies, said in a statement.

Barely a week after oil-producing Nigeria resorted to imports to ease a month-long acute shortage, petrol queues have built up steadily in the city of six million people since Thursday night when some pump stations ran dry.
"People are not taking chances," said one taxi driver.
But PPMC said "There is no need for any panic buying or fear of petrol scarcity."
In its statement, the company detailed a schedule of a total of 107 million litres of petrol to be supplied within the Lagos area between July 9th to next week.

"Thereafter, cargoes of 40 million litres of petrol each will arrive in Lagos in every three days for the rest of the period of July to September, 1997," it said, adding: "There is therefore no need for a mad rush to queue and hoard."
PPMC in June ordered 33 cargoes of petroleum products from Europe to be delivered over the period to September when Nigeria says it will try to repair its own four oil refineries.
"Over the period of July to September, 1997 we will be able to build up our operating stock to eliminate chances of petroleum products supply disruption," PPMC's statement said.

Nigeria, Africa's leading crude oil producer, suffered chaos when a sporadic fuel scarcity that has plagued the nation since January turned into a major crisis in June, crippling public transport and businesses nationwide.
Its four refineries have a combined capacity of 445,000 barrels of crude oil daily but produce only a fraction of that due to deteriorating facilities.
